key_insight: inClinico Agent combines machine-learning trial-success predictions with LLM-based tools to estimate whether phase I–IV studies will meet their primary endpoints.
clinical_relevance: The system could support clinical development prioritization, including oncology, but the abstract reports neither cancer-specific performance nor patient-treatment benefits.
method: Model efficacy and safety/toxicity endpoints separately using registration-time features.
Generate a Predictive Trial Index from 0 to 1 using trial, drug, target and frozen literature-derived features.
Integrate prediction engines with LLMs, retrieval tools and specialized clinical skills.
evidence_signal: For trials initiated in 2021 or later, AUROC was 0.828 for efficacy (n=2,347) and 0.809 for safety/toxicity (n=1,485); ClinicoBench adds 3,235 ongoing trials for prospective tracking.
watch_item: Prospective accuracy remains to be established as ongoing trials complete; AUROC alone does not establish probability calibration or decision-making benefit.
paper_title: inClinico Agent for clinical trial endpoint prediction and prospective evaluation
